intro: Opportunity landed in Meridiani Planum on January 25, 2004 — a hole-in-one that rolled the airbag-bouncing rover directly into a small crater (Eagle Crater) whose walls held the first hematite-rich blueberries ever seen up close on Mars. Designed for 90 sols, Opportunity drove 45.16 km over 14 years until a planet-wide dust storm in June 2018 cut off solar power. Final transmission: "My battery is low and it's getting dark."

Legacy Pan, sols 5084-5111 (May-June 2018) — Opportunity's final 360° panorama before the dust storm. Perseverance Valley descends into Endeavour Crater.
Endeavour Crater rim, where Opportunity spent its final years. The rover's resting spot is in Perseverance Valley to the right.
Hematite "blueberries" — millimeter-scale spherules embedded in Meridiani's bedrock. The first direct evidence of long-duration liquid water on Mars.
